item.title: Golangci Lint Thoughts
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: A while back I added golangci-lint to the github actions of all my projects. I never got around to insuring that they all have compliance, which means a lot of my projects look like this: Which is fine. It’s about gradual improvement when I have time and I am able. However the thing that bugs me about linters is that they have ego creep. WHere it moves away from being about reducing the chance of errors happening, into a world of insuring there are the correct number of new lines between functions.

item.title: Synology and UI text: The Package Manager
item.author: technicalblog123@arran4.com (Arran Ubels)
item.description: One of the major improvements over time has been how text in error messages and other “static” components have become more like read only text box / webpage and interactive over the years. Which means when you get an error message you can copy and paste the text to aid you in your search. This also means that links work. A lot of web pages seem to have failed to grasp this, and have made sections of their application “unselectable”, links “unclickable” and more annoyingly but less importantly, have failed to place white space between distinct elements which means when you go to select text (often by double-clicking and dragging in my case) you “over match” and select elements that are unintended:
